question: If $\Delta_1 = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 \end{vmatrix}$ and $\Delta_2 = \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 6 \end{vmatrix}$ then
explanation:
**Step 1: Evaluate $\Delta_1$**  
$\Delta_1$ is a diagonal matrix. The determinant of a diagonal matrix is the product of its diagonal elements:  
$$\Delta_1 = 1 \times 2 \times 3 = 6$$

**Step 2: Evaluate $\Delta_2$**  
Expand $\Delta_2$ along the first row:  
$$\Delta_2 = 0 \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 \end{vmatrix} - 2 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 6 \end{vmatrix} + 0 \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{vmatrix}$$  
$$= -2(1 \times 6 - 0 \times 0) = -2(6) = -12$$

**Step 3: Compare $\Delta_1$ and $\Delta_2$**  
We have $\Delta_1 = 6$ and $\Delta_2 = -12$.  
Clearly, $\Delta_2 = -2 \times 6 = -2\Delta_1$.  
Thus, $\Delta_2 = -2\Delta_1$, which corresponds to option **B**.
